summary:
[  edit  ]
The Attribute  CHOP  adds, removes or updates attributes of the input  CHOP . Currently there is only one attribute type, a "quaternion". This attribute type is used to group rotation channel triplets (rx,ry,rz) together.
Rotations sometimes need to be grouped together since interpolations on independent X, Y and Z rotations do not produce smooth results. Rotations often need Quaternion interpolation to rotate through the most direct path.
Operations such as resampling and blending recognize the rotation triplet with the "quaternion" attribute. They blend or resample the rotation channels using "spherical linear interpolation". Ordinary interpolation can produce poor blending results, whereas quaternion blending produces the shortest rotation path between two sets of rotations.
See some of the CHOPs that use the attribute: the  Join CHOP ,  Composite CHOP  and  Interpolate CHOP . Other CHOPs may quietly use the Quaternion attribute, such as the  Object CHOP ,  Stretch CHOP  and the  Resample CHOP .
The  Scope  is needed to specify the channels that will be grouped.

parameters.label: Pass Through
parameters.name: pass
parameters.description: Leaves the attributes untouched.

parameters.label: Replace
parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Erases previous attributes and replaces them with the new ones.

parameters.label: Append
parameters.name: append
parameters.description: Keeps previous attributes and combines them with the new attributes. If an attribute already exists on a channel and append attempts to overwrite it, an error will occur.

parameters.label: Remove
parameters.name: remove
parameters.description: Removes all scoped channels' attributes.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the rotation order of the rotation triplet.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method

POPs create and modify 3D data, replacing the older SOPs (Surface Operators) with enhanced performance and flexibility. ## 1. What are POPs? - **Definition**: POPs (Point Operators) are a family of operators in TouchDesigner that run on the GPU, leveraging high parallelism to create and manipulate 3D data efficiently. - **Purpose**: They generate and modify points, primitives, and attributes for rendering (via Render TOP) or output to external devices like LED arrays or lasers. - **Significance**: POPs replace SOPs with GPU acceleration, memory optimization, and integration with modern workflows (e.g., USD, FBX). ## 2.
